svg.text: D2M Test Rig — Target Multi-Agent Architecture
the unit of decomposition is Agent ⊃ Skill (blueprint) ⊃ Tools / MCP (least-privilege capabilities) · each Agent has an AUTHORITY BOUNDARY
AUTHORITY: decompose · route · sequence · run the board · HOLD THE HUMAN GATE · owns NO domain writes
spec → plan → dispatch → review → gate → commit
router · sequential · parallel (board) · loop (critic) · hybrid | reads the Skill Registry as its org chart
Perception / Spec Agent — AUTHORITY: READ-ONLY (interpret design intent) · Skill: image→spec · Tools: vision model · NO SAP writes
DOER AGENTS — domain WRITE authority, each boundary-scoped (least privilege)
REVIEW / BOARD AGENTS — READ + VETO authority, NO writes (run in PARALLEL, then the Conductor synthesizes)
SHARED SUBSTRATE (every agent draws on it)
Model Seam — provider swap · Memory — per-agent ISOLATED context · Learning / MVLL — lessons · Skill Registry — the blueprints = the org chart
EXTERNAL SYSTEMS & CONTRACTS (what the bound tools / MCPs actually reach)
authority boundary ⊃ blueprint of what it can perform ⊃ least-privilege capabilities
An Agent IS: a Skill (its charter) + an authority boundary + a bound, least-privilege tool/MCP set.
The Skill Registry stops being 'things one agent loads' and becomes the ORG CHART of agents.
· Writes are DOMAIN-SCOPED. A reviewer vetoes, never writes. The Material agent cannot touch planning tools.
· The HUMAN GATE exists ONLY at the Conductor — one trust boundary, not many.
· Closes the initial architecture: router + sequential + parallel + loop + hybrid …
… AND adds authority + least privilege = the platform's real governance layer.

Build note (no code today): nothing new under the hood — each Agent = run_turn + isolated memory + its Skill's bound tools; the Conductor is the orchestrator. Authority = which tools a Skill is allowed to bind.
